tasks.short: Agree product specifications with product development colleagues using customer, market and brand evidence.

steps.what: Collect customer feedback, market findings and current specifications.
Prepare a brief linking customer needs to specification choices.

loop.input: Selected consultation evidence, brand guidelines and a brief template.
loop.output: A specification brief with source references, options and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check references resolve; the marketing manager verifies claims, relevance and omitted counterevidence.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per brief; missing evidence stays flagged for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer feedback is free text, and its implications cannot be filled from fixed fields alone.

steps.what: Discuss design, colour, packaging and feasibility trade-offs.
Approve specification changes within agreed product and budget authority.
Record agreed changes, reasons, owners and open questions.
Send the decision summary and follow-up responsibilities.

tasks.design: A small evidence collector assembles permitted records from the {CRM} and {DOCS}; a bounded drafting loop prepares a referenced specification brief. People discuss trade-offs and approve changes, capturing decisions in structured fields that generate the log in {DOCS}, follow-up tasks in {PROJECT} and notifications through {EMAIL}. Start with approved file imports where direct access is unavailable.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered, briefs required contextual reading, and decisions were recorded inconsistently. The discussion itself was never a straightforward automation target.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction, structured templates and ordinary integrations make preparation and recording easier to build. A bounded model can draft the narrative for review.
tasks.still_hard: Customer preferences conflict with manufacturing constraints. Physical samples, aesthetics and uncertain demand still require discussion and testing.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise weak evidence, negotiate trade-offs and judge how a physical product will feel to customers.

ambition.what: Run an evidence-backed packaging review at each prototype milestone.

tasks.altitude: The marketing manager spends less time assembling briefs and chasing decisions. They gain capacity to propose customer tests before specification approval; formal approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Design a customer comparison of two packaging options.
reach.learn: Sampling, neutral questions and the limits of preference evidence.

reach.task: Translate customer requirements into a packaging brief.
reach.learn: Print constraints, accessibility and how to specify visual requirements.

evidence.claim: Evidence collection, template drafting and structured decision records can support human product consultations; this specific design has no documented case in the digest.

assumptions: A typical mid-size company holds feedback in the {CRM} and specifications in {DOCS}.
Time shares are illustrative estimates, with conversation and approval taking most of the task.
The future workflow captures approved decisions in structured fields rather than inferring approval from a transcript.
Build ranges cover one product team and a small set of permitted sources.
unknowns: Where current specifications and customer evidence are actually held.
Who can approve specification changes and within what limits.
Whether exports or interfaces are available to the user.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed implementation.
research_questions: Does the brief preserve conflicting customer evidence as reliably as manual preparation?
Which structured decision fields prevent ambiguity without slowing the meeting?
new_work: Review generated briefs and check source references.
Resolve stale or contradictory product records.
Maintain evidence mappings, templates and access permissions.
Complete structured decision fields during approval.

tasks.short: Recommend product and packaging changes using environmental evidence, commercial constraints and specialist advice.

steps.what: Request material, packaging, production and supplier evidence.
Read evidence and extract material quantities, methods, dates and limitations.

loop.input: Supplier documents and internal evidence for the selected product.
loop.output: An evidence register with values, units, scope, dates, source passages and gaps.
loop.check: Validate units and required fields; a sustainability specialist checks consequential values and comparability.
loop.stop: Two extraction attempts per document; unreadable files and inconsistent evidence go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents vary in wording and layout; fixed fields alone cannot recover scope and caveats.

steps.what: Compare feasible changes using common boundaries, costs and environmental measures.
Draft a recommendation explaining benefits, uncertainty, costs and customer implications.

loop.input: Reviewed option comparison, customer feedback and recommendation template.
loop.output: A referenced recommendation separating measured benefits, assumptions and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Every environmental assertion must match reviewed evidence; the marketing manager checks commercial interpretation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported benefits remain explicit evidence gaps.
loop.why_not_simpler: The recommendation combines contextual customer evidence with technical caveats that a fixed template cannot explain.

steps.what: Discuss feasibility, customer acceptance and environmental trade-offs with technical colleagues.
Approve a pilot or request stronger evidence.
Record the decision, evidence gaps and pilot responsibilities.

tasks.design: A configured request flow in {WORKFLOW} collects approved evidence into {DOCS}, and a bounded extraction loop builds a referenced register. Deterministic calculations compare only specialist-approved, comparable inputs; a second bounded loop drafts the recommendation. People select the pilot, and the approved decision creates responsibilities in {PROJECT}; public environmental claims require a separate publication approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier evidence was inconsistent, comparison boundaries differed, and specialist review was difficult to encode. Drafting recommendations added work without resolving those underlying evidence gaps.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction and drafting can reduce document handling. Reusable calculation templates make assumptions and missing inputs visible.
tasks.still_hard: Reliable lifecycle evidence, burden shifting, supplier verification and customer acceptance remain expensive. Faster drafting does not establish environmental soundness.
tasks.human_edge: Question the comparison boundary, distinguish evidence from claims and balance environmental benefits against practical consequences.

ambition.what: Offer an evidence-backed packaging improvement shortlist for product renewal reviews.

tasks.altitude: The marketing manager brings clearer options and evidence gaps to product discussions. They can propose targeted pilots sooner, while technical validation and investment authority stay with the relevant specialists and approvers.

reach.task: Screen packaging alternatives before commissioning detailed assessment.
reach.learn: Functional units, lifecycle boundaries, uncertainty and evidence quality.

reach.task: Document the evidence supporting a proposed environmental benefit.
reach.learn: Traceable assertions, qualification language and document version control.

evidence.claim: Document extraction and deterministic comparison can support sustainability recommendations, but the digest supplies no product or case validating this application.
Environmental comparisons require compatible boundaries and expert interpretation; extraction alone cannot establish a product's environmental benefit.

assumptions: The marketing manager coordinates recommendations with technical and sustainability colleagues.
Calculations use approved methods and factors; the model does not invent environmental measures.
Time shares retain substantial human evaluation despite opportunities to accelerate drafting.
Build ranges cover a limited product category and exclude commissioning new lifecycle studies.
Access work includes supplier confidentiality and GDPR review where evidence contains personal data.
unknowns: Which supplier evidence is available and licensed for reuse.
Whether an internal or external sustainability specialist can validate comparisons.
Which environmental methods and decision thresholds the company accepts.
Who approves pilots and public environmental claims.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed implementation.
research_questions: Which document types produce reliable extraction of units, boundaries and exclusions?
Which comparison methods suit the selected product category?
What evidence is needed to substantiate the proposed public environmental claims?
new_work: Validate extracted technical values and source passages.
Resolve incompatible comparison boundaries and missing supplier evidence.
Maintain calculation methods, factors and their versions.
Review recommendation drafts and separate pilot hypotheses from publishable claims.

tasks.short: Design and conduct surveys, analyse responses and recommend potential markets.

steps.what: Agree the market question, target population and decision the survey will support.
Design the questionnaire, sampling plan and analysis plan.

loop.input: Survey brief, approved question library and protocol template.
loop.output: A draft questionnaire and analysis outline with sampling assumptions explicitly flagged.
loop.check: The analyst checks neutrality, coverage, answer scales, sampling feasibility and planned interpretation.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions per protocol; unresolved methodological choices remain with the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: New market questions require contextual wording; templates provide structure but cannot settle research validity.

steps.what: Configure questionnaire routing and validation in the {OTHER} survey system.
Pilot the survey and discuss comprehension with selected respondents.
Approve and release survey invitations to the selected sample.
Clean the response export and calculate planned tables and uncertainty measures.
Interpret results and code open responses into a market findings report.

loop.input: De-identified open responses, approved codebook, calculated tables and report template.
loop.output: Response codes, referenced themes and draft findings with sampling limitations.
loop.check: Validate response references and numerical statements; the analyst checks a stratified coding sample and all recommendations.
loop.stop: One coding pass and one correction pass per batch; ambiguous responses remain unclassified for review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Open responses contain varied language; fixed keyword rules miss meaning and cannot reliably explain themes.

steps.what: Judge market attractiveness and recommend a validation experiment.

tasks.design: Configure reusable survey templates and release controls in the {OTHER} survey system, with protocols stored in {DOCS}. A deterministic job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} validates exports and produces planned tables; a bounded loop codes open responses and drafts referenced findings. Analysts validate methodology and interpretation, while the marketing manager approves invitation release and recommends the next market test.
tasks.previous_blocker: Survey software already handled collection, but questionnaire design, export cleaning and narrative analysis remained separate. Reusable analytical routines were costly to assemble for occasional studies.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing survey configuration and quickly built import routines cover much of the repetitive work. A bounded model can propose wording and code open responses under an analyst's protocol.
tasks.still_hard: Recruiting a representative sample, nonresponse bias and the gap between stated interest and purchasing behaviour remain. Faster analysis cannot repair an unsuitable sample.
tasks.human_edge: Ask a commercially useful question, recognise bias and decide what evidence justifies a real market experiment.

ambition.what: Provide a lightweight market screening survey for smaller product teams.

tasks.altitude: The marketing manager can commission smaller studies with clearer decision criteria and spend more time evaluating market experiments. They gain discretion over study sequencing within their existing research budget.

reach.task: Specify a sampling and analysis plan for a market screening survey.
reach.learn: Coverage, nonresponse, weighting and valid uncertainty measures.

reach.task: Design a search demand experiment to test a survey finding.
reach.learn: Intent signals, experiment design and the difference between interest and conversion.

evidence.claim: Survey configuration, reproducible analysis and assisted open-response coding are feasible building blocks; the digest gives no directly matching survey product or case.
Coosto provides social listening and trend monitoring, which can inform survey hypotheses but does not establish representative market demand.
GDPR objections to direct marketing must be respected where survey invitations constitute direct marketing.
The ePrivacy framework governs marketing communications; survey recruitment needs classification rather than an assumption that every invitation is marketing.

assumptions: The manager commissions the study and an analyst handles research design and analysis.
A typical company uses an {OTHER} survey system, with exports sometimes analysed in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Time shares treat design and interpretation as substantial work despite the collection-heavy prior.
No synthetic respondents replace real evidence.
Build ranges cover one survey template family and exclude respondent recruitment and fieldwork.
GDPR review covers purpose, lawful basis, minimisation, retention and processor access; national rules may add requirements for employee surveys.
unknowns: Whether an analyst or research agency supports the manager.
Which survey system, exports and reuse rights are available.
How respondents are recruited and what contact permissions exist.
Whether the target population includes employees or sensitive respondent groups.
Which market decision and budget threshold the study must inform.
research_questions: How closely does assisted coding agree with independent analyst coding?
Which uncertainty measures are valid for the proposed sampling method?
Under the applicable rules, when do the proposed invitations constitute direct marketing?
new_work: Review questionnaire drafts, routing and pilot findings.
Maintain analysis routines, codebooks and survey templates.
Inspect response quality exceptions and coding disagreements.
Monitor sample coverage and nonresponse during fieldwork.
Manage respondent access requests, retention and deletion.

tasks.short: Coordinate promotional events and trade shows, manage commitments and connect attendees with appropriate follow-up.

steps.what: Agree event objectives, audience, success measures and spending limits.
Maintain deadlines, dependencies, responsibilities and readiness checks.
Negotiate delivery details with developers, advertisers, production colleagues and event suppliers.
Approve bookings and purchase commitments within delegated limits.
Prepare the promotional pack from product facts and brand guidance.

loop.input: Approved product facts, event brief, brand guidance and promotional templates.
loop.output: Draft invitation copy, staff briefing and product talking points.
loop.check: Check dates, prices and product claims against records; the marketing manager approves wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per pack; unsupported claims and missing facts go to the owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: The factual fields are deterministic, but audience-specific wording needs contextual drafting.

steps.what: Select the invitation audience and approve the send.
Collect registrations and send confirmations through the {OTHER} event registration system.
Run the event, coordinate colleagues and handle visitors and delivery problems.
Check captured contacts and assign appropriate follow-up owners in the {CRM}.
Review event results and agree improvements for the next event.

tasks.design: Configure event templates, readiness checks and reminders in {PROJECT}, with spending approvals in {PROCUREMENT}. A bounded loop drafts the promotional pack from approved facts; approved invitations run through {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, while the {OTHER} event registration system handles confirmations and capacity. A deterministic connection creates permission-aware follow-up queues in {CRM}, leaving negotiations, live delivery and improvement decisions with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordination crossed suppliers, colleagues and disconnected records. Event tools already handled registration, but plans, promotional preparation and follow-up often needed manual reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow features cover reminders, registration and approvals. Small integrations and a bounded drafting loop can connect the remaining administrative work.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier reliability, live disruptions, personal relationships and the quality of visitor conversations remain human work. Attendance alone does not establish sales impact.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust with partners, read visitors' needs and make calm decisions when delivery changes on the day.

ambition.what: Provide a repeatable small customer demonstration event format for regional teams.

tasks.altitude: The marketing manager spends less time maintaining plans and reconciling attendee records, freeing time for partners and visitors. They can choose more event experiments within existing spending limits; purchasing authority remains unchanged.

reach.task: Build a reusable event readiness and contingency plan.
reach.learn: Venue dependencies, supplier escalation and practical contingency planning.

reach.task: Design an event invitation test and follow-up journey.
reach.learn: Audience selection, communication permissions and measurement beyond attendance.

evidence.claim: Spotler supports marketing journeys and lead management, providing existing components for approved invitations and follow-up.
A vendor case describes DHL eCommerce replacing spreadsheet event administration with Spotler Events; this supports registration feasibility, not a general productivity estimate.
Marketing invitations must follow applicable ePrivacy requirements.
Objections to direct marketing must stop that processing, including related profiling.
Configured plans and deterministic contact routing can reduce administration while live event coordination remains human.

assumptions: The event planner role may be performed by a coordinator in a smaller marketing team.
Time shares describe an event using registration software and a shared project plan; they retain substantial live coordination.
Negotiations establish delivery details; binding purchase commitments pass through the spending approval step.
Registration confirmations are transactional messages using approved templates.
Attendance does not automatically grant permission for marketing follow-up.
Build ranges cover one event format; access work includes GDPR review of attendee data and any national employee consultation requirements.
unknowns: Which event, registration and contact tools are currently used.
Who may approve spending, invitation audiences and external messages.
Whether supplier and registration interfaces are available.
How contacts' permissions and objections are recorded.
Whether regional teams have the staffing and budget to run smaller events.
research_questions: Which event interfaces preserve registration changes and contact permissions reliably?
Which measures distinguish valuable conversations from attendance volume?
Which reminder rules reduce missed dependencies without creating excessive notifications?
new_work: Maintain event templates, dependencies and escalation rules.
Review promotional drafts and approve invitation sends.
Resolve duplicate registrations and uncertain contact permissions.
Monitor failed integrations and follow-up assignment exceptions.
Apply retention rules to attendee and event interaction records.

role.altitude: The marketing manager's week shifts from assembling evidence and coordinating records towards product trade-offs, research quality, pilots and partner relationships. Existing approval limits remain; clearer evidence supports more frequent proposals and smaller experiments.
reach: Work with market research analysts on sampling and evidence quality.
Work with sustainability specialists on comparable environmental evidence.
Work with event planners on repeatable delivery and contingency plans.
Work with advertising and promotions managers on permission-aware audience experiments.
skills_to_grow: Turn a commercial question into a testable decision.
Check sources, uncertainty and contradictory evidence.
Specify deterministic rules and recognise exceptions.
Review model drafts without accepting unsupported claims.
Understand GDPR, applicable ePrivacy requirements and national rules.
Measure commercial outcomes beyond activity counts.
role.ambitious_version: Run a small marketing evidence service that helps product and regional teams choose the next customer test, packaging pilot or event experiment using reusable research, traceable recommendations and explicit spending decisions.
